$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS). See aws/s3.json for the contract.

azure.aks.cluster.crud.title: Managed clusters (create, get, list, delete) over ARM

azure.aks.cluster.power.title: Start / Stop cluster
limitations: Start/Stop update the cluster's logical powerState — there are no real node VMs in-browser to deallocate or boot, so no compute cost changes are simulated, but the API server downtime a Stopped cluster causes IS enforced: runCommand and node-pool writes/deletes are rejected with a 409 until the cluster is started again.

azure.aks.node_pools.crud.title: Node pools (agentPools): add, list, scale, update image, delete
limitations: Scaling, image updates and the autoscaler only change the pool's recorded properties (count, nodeImageVersion, min/max count) — no node VMs are actually provisioned, so the "Nodes" tab is a deterministic rollup of those properties rather than live kubelet-reported node objects. Real Azure's requirement that the cluster be Running before a node pool can be added, scaled or deleted IS enforced (409 ClusterNotRunning while the cluster is Stopped).

azure.aks.cluster_configuration.title: Cluster configuration (Kubernetes version upgrade, automatic upgrade channel, authentication and authorization mode)
limitations: A Kubernetes version "upgrade" updates properties.kubernetesVersion directly (no node-by-node drain/cordon/rolling upgrade is simulated).

azure.aks.run_command.title: Run command (az aks command invoke) — kubectl against the cluster's Kubernetes objects
limitations: Vyomi runs no API server, kubelet or containers: kubectl apply / create / get / describe / delete / scale / version / api-resources work against the objects the cluster stores (manifests from a heredoc, a `cat <<EOF |` pipe or the --file context zip); commands that need running containers or a live API server (logs, exec, port-forward, rollout, top, …) and non-kubectl tools fail with an explanation and a non-zero exit code.
It IS rejected (409 ClusterNotRunning) while the cluster's powerState is Stopped, matching the real requirement for a running API server.

azure.aks.connect_credentials.title: listClusterUserCredential / listClusterAdminCredential (kubeconfig)
limitations: The returned kubeconfig is shaped like the real response (cluster/user/context pointing at the cluster's fqdn) but its certificate and token material is a fixed placeholder, and the server address accepts no real kubectl connections.

azure.aks.namespaces.title: Kubernetes namespaces (create, list, delete)
limitations: Namespaces are modelled as a stateful list on the cluster resource (seeded with the real default/kube-system/kube-public/kube-node-lease set a fresh cluster ships with) — nothing is scheduled into a namespace because there is no live Kubernetes API server behind it. Two things ARE enforced rather than merely stored: the four system namespaces can never be deleted (409 ProtectedNamespace, matching the real 'Managed namespaces' preview), and creating or deleting a namespace is rejected with 409 ClusterNotRunning while the cluster is Stopped, the same API-server-down requirement node pools and runCommand already enforce.

azure.aks.workloads.title: Kubernetes objects: Workloads, Services and ingresses, Configuration (Deployments, Pods, Replica/Stateful/Daemon sets, Jobs, Cron jobs, Services, Ingresses, Config maps, Secrets)
limitations: The objects are real and stored per cluster (applied with kubectl through Run command, or the Apply a YAML dialog, which uses it), listed and deleted for real — but nothing is scheduled: Vyomi doesn't run containers, so controllers create no Pods, workloads report 0 ready replicas, Pods stay Pending (PodScheduled=False) and LoadBalancer Services / Ingresses get no external address.

Roles, ClusterRoles, bindings, ServiceAccounts, NetworkPolicies and Namespaces are stored too (and scanned by Defender for Cloud's Kubescape posture check) but have no dedicated blade; NetworkPolicies are not enforced.

azure.aks.kubernetes_objects.title: Storage (persistent volumes, storage classes), Custom resources, Events
limitations: Persistent volumes / claims / storage classes and custom resource definitions are not kinds Vyomi's Kubernetes object store holds, and with no controllers or kubelet running there are no Kubernetes events to show.

azure.aks.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this cluster
limitations: Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this cluster); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.aks.activity_log.title: Activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.aks.defender.title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (this cluster's recommendations, from Kubescape)
limitations: Shows this cluster's live Defender for Cloud recommendations: Kubescape findings over the Kubernetes objects it stores, while the Containers plan is on — see azure.defender.kubernetes for what each substrate evaluates.
